messages.subject: prediction using counterfactuals
parts:
Hello, 

To assess a model I am running I would like to create predicted values ( + uncertainty) for different scenarios.

For instance, what predicted values would be if a covariate x is set to 1 for all individuals in a dataset. 

This becomes tricky when there are several random effects. 

Do you have any experiences doing something similar? Any examples?

Any help or ideas would be appreciated. 

Thanks so much!
Sebastian

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] prediction using counterfactuals
parts:
On Fri, 2017-02-24 at 14:19 -0800, Sebastián Daza wrote:
> Hello, 
>
> To assess a model I am running I would like to create predicted
> values ( + uncertainty) for different scenarios.
>
> For instance, what predicted values would be if a covariate x is set
> to 1 for all individuals in a dataset. 
>
> This becomes tricky when there are several random effects. 
>
> Do you have any experiences doing something similar? Any examples?
>
> Any help or ideas would be appreciated. 
>

you can do prediction using data=NA,

without prediction:

> n = 10
> x = rnorm(n)
> y = 1 + x + rnorm(n)
> r = inla(y ~ 1 + x, data = data.frame(x,y))

with:

> xx = c(x, 10)
> yy = c(y, NA)
> rr = inla(yy ~ 1 + xx, data = data.frame(xx,yy), control.predictor =
list(compute=TRUE))
> rr$summary.linear.predictor[n+1,]
                    mean          sd  0.025quant    0.5quant  0.975quan
t
predictor.11 15.30355802 2.508233465 10.28985993 15.30268997
20.32579755
                    mode             kld
predictor.11 15.30202064 8.121985705e-07



and you also have the posterior for the linear predictor

H
--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
